If alembic_prime returns recommendedQueries or detailRefs, consume them with alembic_search before coding; use alembic_recipe_map and alembic_graph for ProjectContext navigation and relation evidence.

submitKnowledgeContract.purpose: Prepare valid candidates before the first submit call; rejection remains a safety net, not the normal instruction path.

imperativeVerbs.rule: doClause must start with a positive allowlist verb; dontClause with a negative verb or "Do not …".

evidenceFloor.rule: Rule/pattern candidates need ≥3 distinct source files unless scope: narrow | file-local | local-only; fact candidates need ≥1.

preSubmitChecklist: [stage 1] doClause must start with an English imperative verb from the positive allowlist; dontClause with a negative verb or "Do not …".
[stage 1] Both doClause and dontClause are required, non-empty English imperative clauses.
[stage 1] doClause / dontClause must be English (no Han/Hiragana/Katakana/Hangul script).
[stage 1] content.markdown is required and must include both a ✅ correct and a ❌ forbidden project-specific example (each with ≥4 trailing non-space chars on its line).
[stage 2] Cite concrete repo-relative source refs with a line or line range (lib/module/file.ts:10-18) that resolve to existing files inside the project root.
[stage 2] Rule/pattern candidates need ≥3 distinct source files (unless scope: narrow/file-local/local-only); fact candidates need ≥1.

[stage 2] coreCode / content.pattern must match a cited source line range verbatim (they are project evidence). The markdown code block is a distilled, reusable template — it is NOT checked verbatim, but must not be placeholder code (operation(), doThing, foo, bar, TODO) and its claims stay grounded via (来源: File:行号) refs.

[stage 2] Concrete call-chain claims (caller/callee/call chain/invokes) require fresh graph-backed refs; stale/partial/pending graph evidence is rejected. General dependency/layering/boundary wording does not trigger this gate — its grounding is covered by snippet and source-ref checks.
[stage 2] Cold-start submissions must run inside a bootstrap session whose projectRoot and dimension match the submission.
[stage 3] content.markdown must be ≥200 chars with a code block or file ref; coreCode must not start with a closing bracket; titles must not be generic pattern names.
[stage 3] Title, trigger, and code-fingerprint must be unique against already-submitted recipes (skippable).

fieldFloors.title: Project-local title, <=20 chars when possible, no generic project-name prefix.
fieldFloors.coreCode: 3-8 syntactically complete lines copied or tightly adapted from cited source when code behavior is claimed.
fieldFloors.usageGuide: Markdown with ### When to Use / Key Points / When Not to Use sections.
fieldFloors.reasoningSources: Non-empty repo-relative paths with line ranges matching sourceRefs.
fieldFloors.confidence: recommended >= 0.85 (guidance, not enforced); below it, narrow the candidate or keep analyzing.

sourceRefCardinality.universalRuleOrPattern: >=3 distinct in-scope repo-relative file refs unless scope is explicitly narrow or file-local.
sourceRefCardinality.fact: At least one exact source ref; use more when the fact spans entrypoint, consumer, and validation.
sourceRefCardinality.relationshipClaim: Requires caller/callee/impact/source-node evidence or an explicit raw-read fallback note.

requiredBeforeSubmit: content.markdown includes both ✅ correct and ❌ forbidden project examples
doClause and dontClause are English imperative verb-leading clauses
3-8 line coreCode matching cited source when code behavior is claimed

relationshipGrounding.warningBoundary: Normal submit responses return relationshipGrounding.needs-evidence for unbound relationship claims; session-bound production submissions remain hard-gated by the Recipe evidence gate.

dimensionCompletionContract.sessionField: Use sessionId: bootstrapState.session.id. Do not send bootstrapSessionRef to alembic_dimension_complete; bootstrapSessionRef is accepted by alembic_submit_knowledge only.
requiredBeforeComplete: session-bound Recipe ids returned by alembic_submit_knowledge
current dimension evidence summary tied to submitted sourceRefs
residual risks and next dimension handoff notes

floors.submittedRecipeIds: non-empty ids returned by this bootstrap session; never invent ids from titles

dimensionCompletionContract.checkpointRule: Do not write progress/checkpoint completion when candidate ids, file overlap, findings, source refs, or quality pass are missing.

referencedFiles: repo-relative files used by submitted Recipe sourceRefs
firstCallExample.analysisText: >=500 chars with headings, source summary, and code block where useful

stopConditions: project root or data root mismatch
another bootstrap writer holds the lease
ProjectContext stale/partial/wrong-scope used as final proof
language overlay missing without generic fallback uncertainty
Recipe floor cannot be met and no no-op reason is recorded
runtime transport lacks real MCP readback

submitKnowledgeContract.purpose: Prepare valid candidates before the first submit call; rejection remains a safety net, not the normal instruction path.

imperativeVerbs.rule: doClause must start with a positive allowlist verb; dontClause with a negative verb or "Do not …".

evidenceFloor.rule: Rule/pattern candidates need ≥3 distinct source files unless scope: narrow | file-local | local-only; fact candidates need ≥1.

preSubmitChecklist: [stage 1] doClause must start with an English imperative verb from the positive allowlist; dontClause with a negative verb or "Do not …".
[stage 1] Both doClause and dontClause are required, non-empty English imperative clauses.
[stage 1] doClause / dontClause must be English (no Han/Hiragana/Katakana/Hangul script).
[stage 1] content.markdown is required and must include both a ✅ correct and a ❌ forbidden project-specific example (each with ≥4 trailing non-space chars on its line).
[stage 2] Cite concrete repo-relative source refs with a line or line range (lib/module/file.ts:10-18) that resolve to existing files inside the project root.
[stage 2] Rule/pattern candidates need ≥3 distinct source files (unless scope: narrow/file-local/local-only); fact candidates need ≥1.

[stage 2] coreCode / content.pattern must match a cited source line range verbatim (they are project evidence). The markdown code block is a distilled, reusable template — it is NOT checked verbatim, but must not be placeholder code (operation(), doThing, foo, bar, TODO) and its claims stay grounded via (来源: File:行号) refs.

[stage 2] Concrete call-chain claims (caller/callee/call chain/invokes) require fresh graph-backed refs; stale/partial/pending graph evidence is rejected. General dependency/layering/boundary wording does not trigger this gate — its grounding is covered by snippet and source-ref checks.
[stage 2] Cold-start submissions must run inside a bootstrap session whose projectRoot and dimension match the submission.
[stage 3] content.markdown must be ≥200 chars with a code block or file ref; coreCode must not start with a closing bracket; titles must not be generic pattern names.
[stage 3] Title, trigger, and code-fingerprint must be unique against already-submitted recipes (skippable).

fieldFloors.title: Project-local title, <=20 chars when possible, no generic project-name prefix.
fieldFloors.coreCode: 3-8 syntactically complete lines copied or tightly adapted from cited source when code behavior is claimed.
fieldFloors.usageGuide: Markdown with ### When to Use / Key Points / When Not to Use sections.
fieldFloors.reasoningSources: Non-empty repo-relative paths with line ranges matching sourceRefs.
fieldFloors.confidence: recommended >= 0.85 (guidance, not enforced); below it, narrow the candidate or keep analyzing.

sourceRefCardinality.universalRuleOrPattern: >=3 distinct in-scope repo-relative file refs unless scope is explicitly narrow or file-local.
sourceRefCardinality.fact: At least one exact source ref; use more when the fact spans entrypoint, consumer, and validation.
sourceRefCardinality.relationshipClaim: Requires caller/callee/impact/source-node evidence or an explicit raw-read fallback note.
